passkeys.on-hint: People can add passkeys in their account settings and sign in with them. {{count}} passkeys are registered.
passkeys.off-hint: The sign-in page offers no passkey. The {{count}} registered passkeys are kept and work again once this is back on.
passkeys.rp-hint: A passkey is bound to one domain. Empty uses the domain the page is served from; pin it for a production deployment.
passkeys.rp-id-hint: Such as chat.example.com. In force now: {{current}}. Changing it makes passkeys made for the old domain unusable.
passkeys.rp-id-invalid: Enter a domain, such as chat.example.com
passkeys.origins-hint: One per line, such as https://chat.example.com. Empty: with no domain pinned, the page's own origin; with one pinned, only the server's configured origins (CORS_ORIGINS) within that domain, and the domain itself. In force now: {{current}}.

passkeys.verification-hint: Required asks for a fingerprint, face or device PIN every time; security keys that cannot do that will not work.
passkeys.android-hint: Let OpenChat's Android app sign in with this site's passkeys. One line per signing certificate: the package name and its SHA-256 fingerprint (as keytool -list -v prints it); one line for the release build and one for a debug build. They are published in /.well-known/assetlinks.json.
passkeys.android-apps-hint: Android reads assetlinks.json on the relying party ID's domain to confirm the app may use this site's passkeys.
passkeys.android-pin-rp: Pin the relying party ID to this site's domain above first (now {{current}}): Android reads assetlinks.json on that domain.
passkeys.android-invalid: One package name and one fingerprint per line, separated by a space, such as org.example.openchat AB:CD:… (32 bytes of hex)

system.title: System
system.subtitle: Server-wide settings. They apply to everyone.
system.debug-hint: Logs at debug level, so the terminal shows every step. Takes effect at once, needs no restart, and survives one. Turn it on to chase a problem — it is verbose, and may include request detail.
system.genui-hint: Lets models lay out answers with interface components — cards, figures, tables, steps — for plans, comparisons and checklists. The component guide is added to every request's system prompt, about 2–3k tokens.
system.ask-user-hint: Lets models put multiple-choice questions to the user, and wait for the answers, when they are blocked on a decision that is the user's to make. On by default; for runs in progress it takes effect at their next request.
system.compress-context-hint: When a request would fill more than half of the model's context window (65% once the conversation has a summary), the conversation's own model first summarises the older part, and the model is sent the summary in its place. The original messages stay on screen. A request the model refuses for its length is compressed once and retried at once. Compression is only ever automatic; people cannot compress by hand. Off, requests go out as they are. On by default; runs in progress pick it up at their next request.
system.avatars-hint: Lets people upload a picture of their own in Settings → Account. Off, the button reads "Not available yet" and the first letter of the name is shown. Pictures already set stay, and can always be removed.
system.task-model-hint: The model background tasks use — for now, titling a conversation after its first answer. A cheap, fast model is best. Unset, each conversation's own model is used.
system.memory-hint: When on, the model can remember long-lasting things about a user and use them in later new chats. Off, no chat reads or writes memory; people can still view and delete theirs, and custom instructions are unaffected. On by default. Administrators cannot see anyone's memories.
system.save-failed: Couldn't save the setting. Try again.

run-limit.title: Answers at once
run-limit.intro: An account can have the model writing answers in several conversations at the same time. Each one keeps spending money, so this limits how many.
run-limit.label: Answers at once per account
run-limit.hint: Counted across all the account's conversations. Past it, sending, regenerating, editing and answering a question are refused (try again shortly) and nothing is written. A finished or stopped answer frees its slot at once. Administrators are exempt. 0 is unlimited; the default is 3.
run-limit.required: Enter a number; 0 means no limit

retention.title: Data retention
retention.hint: The server cleans up every 10 minutes. These are how long each kind of data is kept before it goes.
retention.deleted-hint: A conversation a user deleted is kept this long, during which it can still be restored in the database; then it is removed for good with its messages and files.
retention.unsent-hint: Files uploaded in the composer but never sent with a message are removed after this long.
retention.orphan-hint: Files under uploads/ on the local disk that no attachment points to are removed after this long. The data directory must belong to this database alone.

system.allow-registration-hint: Off, the sign-in page stops offering registration and only administrators can add accounts, in Admin → Users. On a fresh install the first account is exempt: it can still register, and becomes the administrator. On by default.
system.approval-hint: On, an account that signs itself up is pending and cannot sign in until an administrator approves it in Admin → Users; accounts an administrator adds need no approval. Only applies while registration is allowed. On by default.
system.approval-off: New users do not need approval
system.tasks-hint: On, people can schedule tasks on the Scheduled tasks page, and models can schedule them for people; each runs in its own conversation in the person's name and counts towards usage as usual. Off, nothing runs (tasks are kept). At most 10 running tasks per person. On by default.
system.traces-hint: On, administrators' own model requests are recorded as sent, with what came back, and an administrator can switch their own conversations to Trace to see timing, tokens and the full request. Only their own conversations; kept for 7 days. For development; off by default. Off, nothing is recorded and the view is hidden.

subagents.enabled-hint: Let models hand self-contained, context-heavy work (researching across many pages, reading a set of sources) to sub-agents, which do it in a context of their own and hand back only a report. Off by default; multi-agent work uses many more tokens, logged as Sub-agent in the usage log.
subagents.model-hint: The model sub-agents use. With “Same as the main model” they use the model of the reply that launched them; to keep costs down, pick a cheaper model and give it a spending cap.
subagents.background-hint: Let the main agent leave sub-agents working in the background while it goes on talking with the user; their reports are delivered when ready. Off, every sub-agent runs in the foreground and the main agent waits for it.
subagents.limits-hint: Sub-agents' runs do not count against a person's own concurrent answers; they are counted here.

channels.title: Channels
channels.subtitle: Connections to model providers.
channels.name: Name
channels.spent-hint: What all of this channel's requests have cost, as the usage log priced them; models without a price add nothing.
channels.base-url-hint: Leave blank to use the provider’s default. A host alone gets the default path (such as /v1) added.
channels.api-key-hint: Leave blank to keep the stored key; it cannot be read back.
channels.api-key-create-hint: Use this key to fetch models. It is saved only when you create the channel. Optional for local services such as Ollama and LM Studio.
channels.delete-confirm: Deletes the channel "{{name}}" and its key. This cannot be undone, but no chat history is affected.
channels.create-failed: Could not create the channel. Check the connection and try again.
channels.update-failed: Could not save the channel. Check the connection and try again.
channels.send-user-id-hint: Adds an anonymous identifier of the user to each request (OpenAI's safety_identifier, Anthropic's metadata.user_id), so an upstream ban can be traced to one user instead of the whole account. It is a keyed hash, never the email. A third-party relay may reject a field it does not know, so this is on by default only for api.openai.com and api.anthropic.com.
channels.models-empty-hint: Fetch the list this endpoint publishes, or add one by hand.
channels.models-fetch-failed: Fetch failed — check the key and the base URL
channels.models-enter-key: Enter an API key to fetch the model list.
channels.models-key-rejected: The endpoint rejected this API key. Check the key and try again.
channels.models-invalid-url: Enter a valid base URL, such as https://example.com/v1.
channels.models-list-empty: The endpoint returned no models. Check the URL, retry, or add a model by hand.
channels.models-unreachable: Could not reach the endpoint. Check the URL and your connection, then retry.
channels.models-invalid: That model selection was refused. Pick at most 2000 models with unique ids.
channels.models-save-connection: Connection details changed. Save them before fetching models.
channels.models-select-hint: Fetch and select the models to connect. Only selected models are saved with the channel and shown on the Models page.
channels.models-limit: You can connect up to {{max}} models to one channel.
channels.api-format-chat-hint: Served by nearly every OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Pick this when unsure.
channels.api-format-responses-hint: OpenAI's newer API. Reasoning models keep their thinking across tool calls; the endpoint must support it.
channels.region-hint: The two sites have separate accounts and keys; pick the one your key is from.
channels.routing-hint: When several channels offer the same model, this decides which is used first. A request that fails before the model has written anything is retried on the next channel.
channels.weight-hint: Among equal priorities, the share of requests: 3 and 1 split about 3:1. 1–1000.
channels.name-taken: Another channel already has this name

models.title: Models
models.subtitle: Only models selected in your configured channels appear here.
models.no-channels: No channels yet. Add one and the models it can reach appear here.
models.no-selected-models: No models connected yet. Fetch and select models in a channel to add them here.

settings.subtitle: Decide how this model is offered. Anything you leave alone follows the model metadata (models.dev).
settings.for-members-hint: Off hides this model from everyone but administrators, and refuses it to them. Administrators and server tasks such as titles keep using it.
settings.kind-hint: Only text models appear in the chat model list, and only they can be chatted with.
settings.tool-hint: Off gives this model no tools — no web search, no page reading.
settings.efforts-hint: Only the checked levels appear in the thinking menu, and requests are checked against them too; Auto is always available. Uncheck all to offer no thinking control.
settings.efforts-unknown: The metadata lists no thinking levels for this model. Checked levels are sent as a reasoning effort, so make sure the model accepts it.
settings.efforts-off: Turn on Reasoning above to choose which thinking levels are offered.
settings.output-hint: Once set, every request carries this limit.
settings.default-value: Metadata default: {{value}}. Leave empty to follow the metadata.
settings.save-failed: Could not save, please try again
settings.reasoning-hint: Off offers no thinking levels; people can only use Auto.
settings.modalities-hint: What the model takes as input; text always.
settings.no-default: The metadata has no figure for this.
settings.capacity-hint: Once this model's spend in the period reaches this amount it can no longer be used. Requests from every user count. Leave empty for no cap.
settings.capacity-invalid: Enter an amount above 0, with at most 6 decimals
settings.period-total-hint: Adds up from a starting point and never clears by itself; "Recalculate" restarts it any time.
settings.period-monthly-hint: Clears at the start of each calendar month, in the time zone the server runs in.
settings.period-daily-hint: Clears at the start of each day, in the time zone the server runs in.
settings.capacity-exempt-hint: While on, administrators can keep using the model once it reaches the cap, and their spend still counts. Off applies the cap to everyone, administrators included.
settings.capacity-recalc-desc: Counting restarts from now: earlier spend no longer counts against the cap, and a model that has reached it is usable again at once. The usage log is untouched.
settings.capacity-no-price: The catalogue has no input or output price for this model (or lists it as free), so its spend is always 0 and the cap can never trigger. Relays and models the catalogue does not list often look like this.
settings.capacity-reset-note: "Restore defaults" also removes the cap and its recalculation point.

models.sync-hint: Model names, context lengths, prices and the like come from models.dev, refreshed daily

image-search.title: Image search
image-search.subtitle: Let answers ask for pictures by description: the model writes what it wants to show ("laptop keyboard") and the server finds a photo in the libraries below, in their order.
image-search.status-live-hint: The model describes pictures; the server finds, downloads and keeps them in file storage, so the same words always show the same picture.
image-search.status-off-hint: Off, the model can show only pictures whose addresses appeared in pages it read or searches it ran.
image-search.provider-hint: Pictures found are downloaded into your file storage; readers' browsers never contact the library.
image-search.order-hint: Asked in order: when one cannot search (an error, a timeout, a rate limit or a missing key) or finds nothing, the next is asked; one that failed lately goes last for a while.
image-search.hint-wikimedia: Wikimedia Commons: no key, fast, documentary photos; no safe-search filter.
image-search.hint-openverse: Openverse: Creative Commons images from many sites with mature content filtered out; no key, but about 200 searches a day per server, and sometimes slow.
image-search.hint-bing: Bing Images: no key, fast, finds nearly anything, with strict safe search; but it is the unpublished endpoint Bing's own page uses, and may stop working or ask for a human check at any time. Pictures come from other sites and keep their rights - they are not freely licensed; check before commercial use.
image-search.hint-pixabay: Pixabay: stock-style photos with safe search; needs a free API key, 100 searches a minute.
image-search.key-stored: A key is stored; only its last four characters are shown.
image-search.key-missing: No key yet: Pixabay cannot search.
image-search.test-hint: Searches once, in the order above or with one service; nothing is kept.

web-search.title: Web search
web-search.subtitle: Let models search the web while they answer. Changes apply from the next model request, including in conversations already running.
web-search.status-live-hint: Models in chat can search the web. Reading a page is always available and obeys the blocklist too.
web-search.status-off-hint: Models are not offered web search. Turn the switch on; Tavily also needs a saved key.
web-search.provider-hint: Searches are run by this service and billed by it.
web-search.tavily-hint: A search API built for AI, returning excerpts and page text.
web-search.key-stored: A key is saved. It cannot be read back; only its last four characters are shown.
web-search.key-missing: No key yet, so web search is unavailable.
web-search.key-removed: Key removed; web search is off
web-search.test-hint: Runs one real search with the saved settings (result count, compression, blocklist) and uses one search credit. An unsaved key typed above is used for the test.
web-search.test-placeholder: What to search for, or leave empty for a default
web-search.results-hint: How much each search returns — and so how many tokens it takes in the model's context.
web-search.max-results-hint: A model may ask for fewer, never more.
web-search.depth-advanced-hint: Excerpts more relevant to the question; two credits a search.
web-search.compression-hint: What each result gives the model. Fuller content grounds the answer better and takes more context.
web-search.compress-snippet-hint: The search service's excerpt; the fewest tokens. The model can still read a page for detail.
web-search.compress-truncate-hint: The page's text cut to a set length; a balance of detail and cost.
web-search.compress-none-hint: The page's whole text, up to 20,000 characters a result. For questions that need close reading.
web-search.blocklist-hint: Blocked sites never appear in results, and models cannot read their pages. One rule per line.
web-search.blocklist-invalid: Line {{line}} is not a valid rule: {{rule}}
web-search.blocklist-rejected: The server could not read a rule in the blocklist; check the regular expressions.
web-search.range: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}
web-search.save-failed: Could not save, please try again
web-search.blocklist-syntax: One per line: a domain (example.com, with its subdomains), a wildcard (*.example.com, subdomains only), or a regular expression between slashes (/\.pdf$/, matched against the whole URL).
web-search.free-hint: The free tiers of Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl and Keenable take turns; when one is rate-limiting or failing, the next one answers. No sign-up and no key, but rate-limited — for light use. Queries are sent to these services.
web-search.depth-free: The free search has no depth setting; this applies to Tavily only.
web-search.compression-free: The free search returns the services' excerpts only; Trimmed and Full use the longer excerpts.

quota.title: Storage per person
quota.hint: What each person uploads - sent or not, in any conversation - may add up to at most this; past it, uploads are refused. A person can be given their own on the Users page.
quota.label: Default limit
quota.description: Every account without its own limit has this one. Lowering it deletes nothing: someone over it can upload again once they delete some files.

storage.title: File storage
storage.subtitle: Where attachments are kept. Changes take effect as soon as you save; no restart needed.
storage.driver-local-hint: Kept on the machine the server runs on. Files are read and written through this server's signed URLs; nothing else to run.
storage.driver-s3-hint: The browser uploads straight to the bucket; file contents never pass through this server.
storage.switch-note: Switching does not strand existing attachments: files already stored are still read from where they are.
storage.local-hint: Files are kept by date in an uploads folder under the directory.
storage.local-dir-relative: A relative path is relative to the server's working directory; the full path is shown once saved.
storage.public-url-hint: Optional. Only needed when the web app and the API are on different origins, e.g. https://chat.example.com. Empty issues relative URLs.
storage.public-url-invalid: Enter an http(s) address with just a scheme, host and port, and no path
storage.dir-note: Changing the directory does not move existing files, and attachments left in the old directory can no longer be read. Copy them to the new one first to keep them.
storage.s3-hint: How to reach the bucket. The secret is write-only and is not shown again once saved.
storage.endpoint-hint: The service's address, e.g. http://localhost:9000 for MinIO or your account's address for R2. Leave empty for AWS S3.
storage.credentials-hint: With the Access Key ID and secret both empty, the server's default AWS credentials are used.
storage.secret-stored: A secret is stored. It cannot be read back, so only its last four characters show. Leave blank to keep it.
storage.path-style-hint: Put the bucket in the URL path rather than the host name. MinIO needs it on; AWS S3 and R2 usually want it off.
storage.cors-title: The bucket must allow cross-origin uploads
storage.cors-note: Browsers PUT files straight to the bucket, so its CORS rules must allow this site's origin (the PUT method and the Content-Type header). Otherwise the browser blocks the upload.
storage.test-hint: Writes a small file with the values currently in the form, reads it back and deletes it. Nothing is saved.
storage.test-ok-hint: Write, read and delete all succeeded.

moderation.intro: Every message and image a user sends goes out under your upstream accounts (OpenAI, Anthropic, a relay), and abusive content can get those accounts banned. With moderation on, each new message is checked before it is sent to a model: one that fails is refused and logged, and someone who keeps failing has their account disabled. Only what a user newly sends is checked (sending, editing, answering the model's question) - not tool results, web pages, earlier turns or titles.

mode.openai-hint: Sends the text and images to OpenAI's moderation endpoint (omni-moderation-latest). Free, about a second; needs an OpenAI API key.
mode.model-hint: Has a model of the catalogue classify the text. It costs model money, shows in the usage log as kind 'moderation' and counts toward the model's spending cap; text only, images are not checked.

form.key-hint: Write-only: it is not shown again after saving, and leaving the box empty keeps the stored one. Used for the moderation endpoint only.
form.base-url-hint: Empty is OpenAI's own address; for a relay, its /v1 address.
form.model-hint: A cheap, fast model is best. It is a server task like the task model, so 'open to regular users' does not apply. While the model is at its spending cap the check is unavailable, and 'When moderation is unavailable' below applies.
form.model-unavailable: That model is not available right now. Choose another.
form.categories-hint: A message that matches any chosen category is refused. The categories are those of OpenAI's moderation model.
form.min-score-hint: At 0 only what the service flagged counts. Above 0, a chosen category whose score reaches it blocks too, flagged or not - it can only make the check stricter.
form.exempt-admins-hint: Off by default: an administrator's messages reach the same upstream accounts and are checked too. Administrators are only logged, never disabled automatically.
form.on-error-hint: What happens to an account's message when the service errors, times out, has no channel or the model is at its cap.
form.url: Enter an http(s) address, or leave it empty
form.key-required: This mode needs an OpenAI API key

sanctions.title: Sanctions
sanctions.hint: When an account has this many messages refused within the window, it is sanctioned: the account is disabled and signed out. The count starts over after a sanction.
sanctions.strikes-hint: How many refused messages set it off. 0 never sanctions and only logs. Administrators are only logged.
sanctions.strikeWindowHours-hint: Only refused messages this recent count.

source.document: Writing block, before a model read it

log.subtitle: Messages moderation refused: who sent them, which categories matched, the start of the text. Only refused messages are logged, for 90 days, and only administrators can see them.

usage.subtitle: Every request made to a model: who sent it, through which channel, what it cost and how fast it came back.
usage.price-hint: USD per 1M tokens, input / output, as priced when the request was made
usage.estimated-hint: The provider did not report this request's usage (it was stopped, cut off, or the provider reports none), so the token counts and cost are the server's estimate, which errs high. Whatever the provider did report is kept as it is.
usage.speed-hint: Output tokens over the whole request, the wait for the first token included. Not shown for tiny, failed or estimated requests.
usage.no-duration: The provider rejected the request at once; no time was spent

personalization.instructions-hint: Write what you want the model to always know and follow. Every new chat starts with them, temporary chats included.
personalization.about-placeholder: For example: I'm a backend engineer working mostly in Go and PostgreSQL.
personalization.style-placeholder: For example: lead with the conclusion, then explain; keep answers short.
personalization.memory-admin-off: An administrator has turned memory off: no chat reads or writes it for now. You can still view and delete your memories.
personalization.memory-temporary: Temporary chats never read or write memory; they only use the custom instructions above.
personalization.memory-description: Add memories with Manage below to make the model more helpful and tailored to you. The model also keeps notes worth remembering on its own as you chat, tells you in its reply, and you can undo it.

refused.blocked: This text did not pass content moderation and was not saved. Please change it and try again.
refused.unavailable: Content moderation is unavailable right now, so this was not saved. Try again later.

memory.full: Memory is full ({{max}} notes). Delete or tidy some first; the model won't add new ones either.
memory.full-error: Memory is full. Delete some first.
memory.empty: No memories yet. The model notes what is worth keeping during chats, and you can add your own.
memory.undo-changed: Can't undo: the memory was changed since.
memory.too-long: A memory can be at most 200 characters.
memory.title: Memory
memory.editor-hint: One lasting fact or preference, in a sentence. ⌘/Ctrl + Enter saves.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.desc: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN instead of a password. Passkeys live on your devices or in your password manager.
passkeys.add-failed: The passkey could not be added. Try again.
passkeys.exists: This device already has a passkey for your account.

account.name: Username
account.name-hint: You can sign in with your username or email.
account.password-hint: Other devices will be signed out; this one stays signed in.
account.title: Your account
account.new-placeholder: Enter a new password (8 characters or more)
account.avatar-hint: PNG, JPEG or WebP; the middle of the image is cut to a square. Without one, the first letter of your name is shown.
account.avatar-type: Choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP image.
account.avatar-too-large: That image is too large. Choose one under 10 MB.
account.avatar-failed: The picture could not be saved. Try another image.

data.storage-full: Your storage is full. Delete files you no longer need to upload again.
data.storage-nearly-full: Your storage is nearly full. You can delete files you no longer need in the library.
data.temporary: Temporary chats are deleted 24 hours after they start.
data.export-desc: Downloads a JSON file with every chat you keep and, for each, its messages. Temporary chats and the tool calls behind answers are not in it.
data.export-failed: The export failed. Please try again.
data.delete-desc: Deletes all of your chats, temporary ones included. This cannot be undone.
data.delete-confirm: Delete all your chats? This cannot be undone.

library.title: Library
library.empty-hint: Images and PDFs you send in conversations show up here.
library.retry: Couldn't load files. Click to retry
library.delete-description: “{{name}}” will be deleted for good. Its message will show it as deleted, and models can no longer read it. This can't be undone.

tasks.title: Scheduled tasks
tasks.off: Scheduled tasks are turned off by an administrator
tasks.retry: Couldn't load tasks. Click to retry
tasks.empty-hint: Have a model do things for you at set times: a daily briefing, a weekly review, a reminder.
tasks.ask-hint: You can also just say in a chat: “send me a news summary every morning at 8”.
tasks.delete-description: “{{title}}” will no longer run. Its conversation and what it wrote there stay.

field.title: Name
field.prompt-placeholder: e.g. Find today's five most important tech stories and summarise each in one sentence.
field.prompt-hint: At each run this is sent in your name to the task's own conversation. The model sees no other conversation, so make it complete.
field.month-end: In a month without that day, it runs on the last day.

error.too-many: You have the most running tasks allowed. Pause or delete one first
error.blocked: Content moderation refused this task. Please change it
error.moderation: Content moderation is unavailable. Try again later
error.busy: The task's conversation is answering. Try again shortly
error.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again

reason.model_capacity_reached: the model's budget was used up
reason.revise_refused: a refused message in its conversation needs rewording
reason.missed: the server couldn't run it on time, so it was skipped

news.title: Daily news briefing
news.hint: The news worth knowing, every morning.
news.prompt: Find today's five most notable news stories (covering tech, business and world news), summarise each in a sentence or two, and link the sources.

weekly-review.title: Weekly review
weekly-review.hint: Look back on your week on Friday evening.
weekly-review.prompt: Help me review my week: ask a few questions about what I got done, what got in the way, and the three most important things for next week.

learn.title: Something new every day
learn.prompt: Teach me one interesting and useful fact from a random field, in plain words, with an everyday example.

meals.title: Weekly meal plan
meals.hint: Plan the week's meals and a shopping list.
meals.prompt: Plan seven healthy dinners for next week with short instructions for each, then a shopping list grouped by category.

deals.title: Flight price watch
deals.hint: Check fares on a route you care about every week.
deals.prompt: Search for current round-trip fares from New York to London and tell me the typical price range and the cheapest departure dates.

monthly.title: Start-of-month money check
monthly.hint: On the 1st, a reminder to tidy your finances.
monthly.prompt: Remind me to do my start-of-month finances: review last month's spending, check auto-renewing subscriptions, set this month's budget, with a short checklist.

trace.empty: No trace for this conversation yet
trace.empty-hint: Only administrators' own requests are recorded, for {{days}} days; earlier ones were not.
